Beszterec Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Beszterec, Hungary

Demolished. Beszterec's Jewish cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, its earliest documented reference. The village itself has ancient roots, referenced in pre-1290 documents as 'Biztitch,' and its population was predominantly Hungarian Calvinist. Only three Jewish families lived there before 1871; the community grew modestly to 24 (of 366 residents) by 1880 and 66 (of 979) by 1910. Jewish residents came to dominate the local fishing trade in the late 18th century, supplying towns as far as Debrecen and Oradea - fish and palinka (brandy) were local dietary staples. Beszterec's Jewish community fell under the religious jurisdiction of Kemecse, and its Jews were deported during World War II via Nyíregyháza. The cemetery was demolished at an unrecorded time and built over.
